confirmed.issue: The stack cannot be built with the Node version available on the implementation machine: Astro 7.4.1 (current latest stable) requires Node >=22.22.0 and aborts on older 22.x, while the machine runs v22.14.0 and the design only says "Node 22".
confirmed.evidence: `node --version` returns v22.14.0 in the repo environment. `npm view astro version` returns 7.4.1 and its package.json declares `engines.node: ">=22.22.0"`. Running the installed Astro 7.4.1 CLI prints `Node.js v22.14.0 is not supported by Astro! Please upgrade Node.js to a supported version: ">=22.22.0"` and exits before build. design.md §6.2 specifies only `Node 22`.
confirmed.suggestion: Pin the Node floor (>=22.22.0, or Node 24 LTS) in `.nvmrc`, `package.json#engines`, and `actions/setup-node` via `node-version-file`; pin Astro and @astrojs/mdx versions with a committed lockfile.

confirmed.issue: ProjectLayout's "MDX body, media gallery" composition cannot represent the existing pages' interleaved text and media; rendering the flat `media[]` array after the body reorders most content and violates the desktop parity contract.
confirmed.evidence: `/Users/xiaoxia/Development/portfolio/website/word-to-world.html` alternates headings/text with images and videos (lines 46-59, 62-81, 110-121); `coffee-composer.html` interleaves text, images and videos (lines 35-46, 57-64, 87-144). design.md §3.5 assigns ProjectLayout the responsibilities "MDX body, media gallery"; the §3.3 `media` array has no position relative to body blocks, and §5.2 requires identical desktop rendering.
confirmed.suggestion: Choose the model explicitly: import VideoPlayer/ResponsivePicture inline in each MDX entry and treat `media[]` as an optional end gallery, or add ordered content blocks/sections to the schema. Document which one ProjectLayout renders.

confirmed.issue: With `build.format: 'directory'`, Astro does not emit redirect pages at the legacy `.html` paths; it emits `<legacy-path>/index.html`, so the old URL resolves only through host-level directory canonicalization.
confirmed.evidence: A build of the exact §6.1 config with Astro 7.4.1 produced `dist/about/about.html/index.html` and `dist/word-to-world.html/index.html` (build log: `/about/about.html/index.html`), while design.md §3.4 says Astro "emits meta-refresh pages at the old paths". GitHub Pages must 301 `/about/about.html` to `/about/about.html/` for the stub to be reached. In dev, Astro compiles the redirect route pattern with `trailingSlash: 'always'` (requiring a trailing slash), and the dev trailing-slash middleware exempts paths with a file extension, so the unslashed legacy URL does not match.
confirmed.suggestion: Emit exact stubs: generate them from the collection with a prerendered endpoint such as `src/pages/[...legacy].ts` (verified to produce `dist/word-to-world.html`), or place static files under `public/`. Otherwise document reliance on GitHub Pages' implicit 301 and change acceptance check 2 to request `<legacy>.html/`.

confirmed.issue: The media schema cannot express what the components are specified to render: no controls/autoplay/loop/muted flags, no width/height or aspect ratio, and no mechanism to select the 480p rendition.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §3.3 media objects contain only `type`, `src`, `poster`, `alt`, `caption`. §3.5 says VideoPlayer supports autoplay/loop/muted and ResponsivePicture emits "explicit dimensions"; §4.2 produces `video-720.mp4` and `video-480.mp4`. Existing pages need both playback modes: `word-to-world.html:81` uses `controls`, while `word-to-world.html:112` uses `autoplay loop muted`.
confirmed.suggestion: Add `controls`, `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `playsinline`, and `width`/`height` (or `aspectRatio`) to the media schema, and define how VideoPlayer chooses between 480p and 720p, or drop the 480p output.

confirmed.section: §3.4 Routing / §3.2 Directory layout (dynamic [slug] vs dedicated pages)
confirmed.issue: Project routes and dedicated site pages share the root namespace; when a project slug matches a site page route, Astro keeps the static page and drops the project page with only a warning.
confirmed.evidence: An Astro 7.4.1 build with `about.astro` and `[slug].astro` returning `slug: 'about'` logged `[WARN] [build] Could not render '/about' from route '/[slug]' as it conflicts with higher priority route '/about'` and emitted only about.astro. Astro 7's default `prerenderConflictBehavior` is `warn`. The current set has the near miss `/painting/` (painting.html) versus `/paintings/` (paintings/indexpainting.html).
confirmed.suggestion: Set `prerenderConflictBehavior: 'error'` in astro.config.mjs and add a reserved-site-route check or test (about, contact, design, paintings, poems) so a new MDX file cannot silently lose its page.

confirmed.issue: The carousel and other third-party runtime dependencies cannot be preserved by "small vanilla TypeScript modules" as described, and several are missing from the interaction and external-reference audits.
confirmed.evidence: `photography.html:110-112`, `painting.html:98-100` and `printing.html:98-100` load jQuery 1.11.0 from code.jquery.com and slick 1.6.0 from cdn.jsdelivr.net before `carousel.js`; `carousel.js:6` calls `$('.slider').slick(...)`. `paintings/indexpainting.html:6-14,23` loads Bootstrap 3.3.6 from maxcdn and uses `data-ride="carousel"`. `contact/contact.html:6` loads Font Awesome from maxcdn. `index.html:305,314,323` reference `78.media.tumblr.com` (not the audited `media.tumblr.com`), and `index.html:324-326` embeds a dead HTTP Xiami Flash player.
confirmed.suggestion: Vendor jQuery+slick and Bootstrap, or scope an explicit vanilla carousel rewrite with behavior tests; add every CDN/host to the media audit and to acceptance criterion 3.

confirmed.section: §3.5 ProjectCard / §3.3 cover / §5.1 Layout rules / §5.2 Desktop parity
confirmed.issue: The single ProjectCard/cover/order model and the prescribed uniform auto-fit grid cannot reproduce the home page's three distinct project-link treatments or its fixed-width desktop layout.
confirmed.evidence: `index.html:61-146` renders 9 selected-work cards with per-project thumbnails including animated GIFs (`foxThumb.gif` line 62, `bird_above_sea.gif` line 78); `index.html:158-198` renders 8 round-masked prototype GIF links; `index.html:240-249` renders 3 more circular links. design.md §3.3 has one `cover` object and one `order`; §3.5 lists only ProjectCard. §5.1 prescribes `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))` and a 1200px container, while §2.3 records existing 378/768/960px fixed widths and §5.2 requires identical rendering at >=1200px.
confirmed.suggestion: Add home-presentation fields (section, thumbnail kind image/video, per-section order) and separate components for selected cards, prototype tiles and what's-more links; scope §5.1's grid/container rules below 1200px or renegotiate the parity contract.

confirmed.issue: The deploy workflow leaves the Pages artifact path unspecified, but `actions/upload-pages-artifact` defaults to `_site/`, not Astro's `dist/`, so the deploy job fails.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §6.2 lists only `actions/upload-pages-artifact` then `actions/deploy-pages`, while §3.2/§6.1 build to `dist/`. The `actions/upload-pages-artifact` action.yml declares `path` with `default: "_site/"`.
confirmed.suggestion: Add `with: { path: dist }` to the upload step, include the `github-pages` environment on the deploy job, and verify Settings -> Pages -> Custom domain still shows xinyue.de after switching the source to GitHub Actions.

confirmed.issue: The publish step specifies no artifact path. actions/upload-pages-artifact defaults to `_site/`, while Astro emits `dist/`; implemented literally, the upload step fails. Copying the official starter workflow's `path: '.'` instead uploads the repository root, which at cutover still contains the old root index.html, so Pages would keep serving the old site instead of the Astro build.
confirmed.evidence: Design 6.2 says only "Publish: `actions/upload-pages-artifact` then `actions/deploy-pages`"; design 6.1 sets no `outDir`. `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5.0.0/action.yml` declares `path` default `_site/`; Astro 7.4.1 `dist/core/config/schemas/defaults.js` has `outDir: './dist'`. The GitHub starter `pages/static.yml` uses `path: '.'` (entire repository).
confirmed.suggestion: Specify `with: path: ./dist` (or use `withastro/action`, which handles the Astro output) and assert the artifact contains `index.html` and `_astro/` before deploying.

confirmed.issue: `workflow_dispatch` has no ref guard and there is no environment protection, so selecting `astro-rebuild` in the Run workflow UI deploys unfinished work directly to the live custom domain. GitHub also only exposes `workflow_dispatch` once the workflow file exists on the default branch (`master`), so there is no safe pre-merge preview path.
confirmed.evidence: Design 6.2: "Trigger: push to `master`, plus `workflow_dispatch`"; design 6.3 says development happens on `astro-rebuild`. Repo: `git branch -a` shows `astro-rebuild` and `master` with `origin/HEAD -> origin/master`, and `astro-rebuild` has no upstream. GitHub docs: "To trigger the workflow_dispatch event, your workflow must be in the default branch." The design defines no `github-pages` environment or protection rule.
confirmed.suggestion: Gate the deploy job with `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'` and/or add a `github-pages` environment protection rule that only allows `master`; use a separate non-production target if previews are needed.

confirmed.issue: The cutover order is wrong: Phase 5 merges to `master` first and then enables GitHub Actions as the Pages source. The merge push triggers the workflow while Pages is still "Deploy from a branch", so deploy-pages fails with "Get Pages site failed". During that window the same push is eligible for a Jekyll build of the Astro tree (no root index.html; `_astro/` is underscore-prefixed and excluded by Jekyll), which can take the live site down. Acceptance criterion 8 cannot be exercised before merge because `workflow_dispatch` requires the workflow on `master`.
confirmed.evidence: Design 6.2: "Repository setting: Settings -> Pages -> Source = GitHub Actions. This is a one-time manual change." Phase 5: "Merge to master, enable GitHub Actions as the Pages source, and confirm the production deploy." Criterion 8: "The GitHub Actions workflow deploys successfully to Pages." GitHub docs: "To start using custom workflows you must first enable them for your current repository"; the deploy-pages first-run failure on an unconfigured Pages site is a known error. The live site is currently branch-published (`last-modified: Mon, 03 Jun 2024`, root `CNAME`).
confirmed.suggestion: Reorder: land the workflow on `master` without deleting old files, switch Settings > Pages to GitHub Actions, push/merge to run the first Actions deploy, verify, then delete old source/media in a follow-up commit. Never leave a branch-based build pointed at an Astro-only tree.

confirmed.issue: The Node version is not pinned to Astro 7's requirement. Astro latest (7.4.1) declares `node >=22.22.0`, but the local environment is Node 22.14.0/npm 10.9.2, below the floor, and the design only says "Node 22" with no `.nvmrc`, `engines`, or setup-node step.
confirmed.evidence: Astro 7.4.1 `package.json` engines `{node: '>=22.22.0'}`; `node -v` returns v22.14.0 and `npm -v` returns 10.9.2. Design 3.1 says "Astro (latest stable)" and design 6.2 says "Node 22"; actions/setup-node is not mentioned in 6.2.
confirmed.suggestion: Pin one supported Node line for local and CI (Node 24 LTS, or Node 22.23.x with npm 11.3+), add `.nvmrc` and `engines`, and use actions/setup-node with `node-version-file: .nvmrc`.

confirmed.issue: Even with a lockfile, `npm ci` on the Ubuntu runner can fail because Node 22 ships npm 10.9.x, whose optional-dependency resolution bug can omit Linux native packages from a macOS-generated lockfile. Astro 7 pulls Vite 8/rolldown and lightningcss (per-platform optional dependencies) plus optional sharp.
confirmed.evidence: Node v22.23.4 bundles npm 10.9.9; Node v24.10.0 bundles npm 11.6.1 (nodejs/node tags). Astro 7.4.1 depends on `vite ^8.3.4`; `rolldown@1.2.12` lists `@rolldown/binding-linux-x64-gnu` as an optional dependency, `lightningcss@1.33.0` lists `lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu`, and `sharp@0.35.4` lists `@img/sharp-linux-x64`. The npm bug is reported fixed in npm 11.3.0 (npm/cli#8184); the local npm is 10.9.2.
confirmed.suggestion: Use Node 24 with npm >=11.3 in CI, or regenerate the lockfile in a Linux container; add a CI smoke test that runs `npm ci` on `ubuntu-latest` before the first Pages deploy.

confirmed.section: 6.3 Branch and release; 9 Risks and rollback
confirmed.issue: Custom-domain/CNAME behavior across the source switch and rollback is unaddressed. GitHub ignores a repository CNAME for Actions deployments and uses Settings > Pages; the design never verifies the domain survives the switch. The rollback is not executable as written: `pre-astro` is a tag, and Pages branch publishing accepts a branch, not a tag; after the merge `master` contains the Astro tree, so "set Pages back to the previous source" would publish the new tree. If the custom domain is lost, Pages serves at `softlipaschara.github.io/website/`, while Astro emits root-absolute `/_astro/...` assets (base `/`), breaking the site.
confirmed.evidence: Design 6.3: "tag `pre-astro` at the current master commit"; Section 9: "set Pages back to the previous source and force-push nothing". Repo: `git ls-files` shows a tracked root `CNAME`; design 3.2 `public/` lists only `assets/ui/`, with no CNAME; default branch is `master`. GitHub docs: for a custom Actions workflow "no CNAME file is created, and any existing CNAME file is ignored and is not required"; the custom domain is configured in settings.
confirmed.suggestion: Record the current custom domain and Enforce HTTPS state before switching and verify both after; create and push a `pre-astro` branch at the tag, and document rollback as switching Pages to that branch (root) or reverting the merge on `master`. Keep `CNAME` on the rollback branch.

confirmed.issue: Astro 7 with `build.format: 'directory'` emits redirect stubs as directories: `/about/about.html` becomes `dist/about/about.html/index.html`, not `dist/about/about.html`. GitHub Pages serves exact `.html` files directly and normalizes directories with a 301 (`/folder` -> `/folder/`), but the design never verifies that an extension-bearing path backed by a directory resolves. Local `dist`/`astro preview` checks do not reproduce Pages routing, so acceptance criterion 2 (all legacy `.html` URLs) can ship broken or with an extra redirect hop. The extensionless forms GitHub Pages also served via its `.html` rule (`/about/about`, `/breathing-surface`) are not in the redirect map.
confirmed.evidence: Astro 7.4.1 `dist/core/build/common.js`: for `buildFormat: 'directory'`, `getOutFolder` returns `dist/<pathname>/` and `getOutFile` returns `index.html`. Simon Willison's GitHub Pages manual: `/foo.html` serves the file, `/folder` 301s to `/folder/`, and custom redirects are not supported. Live `curl -I https://xinyue.de/paintings` returns `301 location: https://xinyue.de/paintings/`. Design Phase 5 only says "Serve `dist/` locally and run link, redirect, and media checks."
confirmed.suggestion: Validate every legacy URL (both `.html` and extensionless forms) on a real Pages deployment before cutover, or generate flat `dist/<legacy>.html` stubs with a post-build copy and remove the corresponding Astro redirect entries (a file and a directory with the same name cannot coexist).

confirmed.issue: The design relies on `media-src/`, `media-out/`, and `public/media/` being gitignored but never updates `.gitignore`, which currently contains only `.idea/` and `.DS_Store`; `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.astro/`, and `.env.local` are also missing. The repository pack is already 514.77 MiB; committing node_modules or media directories would push it toward/over GitHub's 1 GB recommended Pages source limit and bloat every Actions checkout. A committed `public/media/` would also be copied into `dist/`, inflating the Pages artifact toward the 1 GB published-site limit and 10-minute deployment timeout.
confirmed.evidence: `.gitignore` contains only `.idea/` and `.DS_Store`. `git count-objects -vH` reports `size-pack: 514.77 MiB`; the GitHub API reports repo `size: 527050` KB. Design 4.2 says media-src/media-out are "(gitignored)"; design 4.5 says `public/media/` is "(gitignored)"; no phase lists a `.gitignore` change. GitHub Pages limits: published site <=1 GB and deployment timeout 10 minutes.
confirmed.suggestion: Add `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.astro/`, `.env.local`, `media-src/`, `media-out/`, and `public/media/` to `.gitignore` in Phase 1, verify before the first push, and add a pre-merge check that `dist/` stays small.

confirmed.issue: The per-project object scheme uses one fixed video name, one fixed poster name, and one fixed GIF output name, but the schema and the real content have many media items per project, so a literal implementation overwrites every video and poster with the last one processed.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.1 (lines 302-310) defines exactly projects/<slug>/video-720.mp4, video-480.mp4, and poster.jpg; §4.2 (lines 331-347) writes those fixed names plus loop.mp4 for GIFs. §3.3 (lines 216-225) defines media as an array. In the repo, /Users/xiaoxia/Development/portfolio/website/word-to-world.html has 27 unique media sources, scribbling-speech.html 18, ink-animation.html 8 GIFs, jie.html 5, omzug.html 5, and breeze.html 5. ink-animation.html alone would map 8 different GIFs to the same loop.mp4.
confirmed.suggestion: Give every media item a stable id in frontmatter and key every output by it, for example projects/<slug>/<media-id>/<media-id>-720.mp4, <media-id>-480.mp4, <media-id>-poster.jpg, <media-id>-800.webp; define the mapping in the schema and in optimize.sh, and update §4.1/§4.2 accordingly.

confirmed.issue: The pipeline generates and uploads two renditions, but the schema exposes only one src and no component selects between 720p and 480p, leaving the 480p files unreferenced.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §3.3 (lines 216-225) has media[].src as a single string; §4.1 (lines 303-304) lists both video-720.mp4 and video-480.mp4; §4.2 (lines 331-337) generates both; §3.5 (line 274) describes VideoPlayer without any source-selection behavior. The HTML <source media> attribute is ignored for <video> in browsers, so a naive <source media=...> would not solve it.
confirmed.suggestion: Either drop the 480p rendition or add explicit src720/src480 (or a renditions object) to the schema and select in VideoPlayer with matchMedia/navigator.connection; document the chosen policy.

confirmed.issue: The reference poster command fails for videos shorter than one second, and the pipeline defines no failure behavior.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.2 (line 339) uses ffmpeg -ss 1 -i input.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 poster.jpg. /Users/xiaoxia/Development/portfolio/website/imgA/speechdetection.mp4 is 0.40 s; running that exact command exits 234 with 'Nothing was written into output file' and produces no poster. If the script uses set -e the whole run stops; if not, a stale poster.jpg from a previous item can be reused. imgA/cloudy.mp4 is 1.03 s and succeeds.
confirmed.suggestion: Compute min(1, duration*0.5) with ffprobe and pass it to -ss (or use -ss 0), check exit status and output existence, fall back to a placeholder or the first frame, and generate posters per media item (see the naming finding).

confirmed.issue: The first-frame-at-1s poster rule discards the 13 existing curated posters and the 13 Vimeo thumbnails, changing rendered pages and violating the desktop-parity contract.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.2 (lines 326 and 339) generates poster.jpg for every video. Current HTML has 13 poster= attributes: imgA/bearPoster.png, box_view_poster.png, breezeVideoBackground.png, cowboyPoster.png, elephantPoster.png, mushroomPoster.png, poster_cat_story.png, poster_chinese.png, poster_chinese_video.png, poster_visualisation_video.png, transcript_poster.png, user_interaction_poster.png, videoPoster.jpg. /Users/xiaoxia/Development/portfolio/media-src/ also contains 13 Vimeo thumbnail JPGs. §5.2 (lines 417-427) permits only anti-aliasing, removed comments, and already-broken images as differences.
confirmed.suggestion: Prefer an explicit poster from frontmatter, then the source's existing poster/Vimeo thumbnail, and only fall back to frame extraction; add a poster column to media-audit.md and migration-checklist.md.

confirmed.issue: There is no source for intrinsic image and video dimensions, so ResponsivePicture's explicit dimensions and §5.1's aspect-ratio wrappers cannot be generated in the CI build.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §3.3 (lines 212-225) has only src, poster, alt, and caption; §3.5 (line 275) promises explicit dimensions; §5.1 (line 413) promises aspect-ratio wrappers. The media files live in gitignored media-out/ (§4.2 line 318), and the GitHub Actions build (§6.2 lines 471-474) only runs npm ci and npm run build, so it cannot probe the files. Without dimensions, images and videos render without width/height and cause layout shift.
confirmed.suggestion: Generate a committed media-manifest.json (key, width, height, bytes, variants, hash) in the media pipeline and consume it in the schema/components, or add width/height to frontmatter with zod validation.

confirmed.issue: No build-time or post-deploy check verifies that every frontmatter media reference exists, so broken media can ship while npm run build and the no-broken-internal-links criterion still pass.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §3.2 (lines 181-185) lists scripts/media/audit.mjs without a contract; §7 Phase 3 (line 518) says 'Audit every media reference' and line 523 says 'verify a sample of objects'; §8 criterion 7 (line 560) only checks internal links. Because media URLs are external, Astro's build cannot detect a 404. The repo already has 19 local refs that are absent (see the next finding).
confirmed.suggestion: Make audit.mjs mandatory and deterministic: parse every MDX cover.src, media[].src, and poster, assert each key exists in media-out/ or the manifest, and run a post-upload HEAD/GET spot-check (or full key listing) before deploying; fail the workflow on any miss.

confirmed.section: §2.4 Known broken or stale items / §10 Dependencies and open inputs
confirmed.issue: The known-broken list omits 19 missing local media references across 8 pages, including an entire paintings gallery.
confirmed.evidence: Cross-checking all src/poster attributes against the filesystem in /Users/xiaoxia/Development/portfolio/website found 19 missing refs on 8 pages: paintings/indexpainting.html (6), scribbling-speech.html (5: bouncing.gif, jumping.gif, running.gif, size.png, poetry.jpg), jie.html (2: papercut.png, face.png), word-to-world.html (2: imgA/bigbuckbunny.mp4, imgA/catWalking.mp4), and one each in about/about.html, coffee-composer.html, painting.html, poems/indexpoem.html. Sampled live URLs (https://xinyue.de/imgA/hanwen.jpg, /imgA/bigbuckbunny.mp4, /imgA/bouncing.gif, /imgA/papercut.png, /imgA/media_photo_coffee.jpg, /imgA/self.jpg) all return 404. §2.4 (lines 123-131) and §10 (lines 590-591) mention only self.jpg and Instagram.
confirmed.suggestion: Add the full per-page missing-asset inventory to §2.4/media-audit.md and choose an explicit outcome for each: owner supplies, omit with an editorial note, or a documented placeholder. Do not let the migration silently drop them.

confirmed.section: §2.2 Media inventory / §4.7 Vimeo source availability / §7 Phase 3
confirmed.issue: External media recovery assumptions are wrong and the design has no policy or schema state for unrecoverable source media.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §2.2 (lines 94-101) and §7 (line 519) assume S3/Tumblr media can be downloaded; §4.7 provides a fallback only for Vimeo. HTTP checks: all 7 s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/omzug.com URLs return 403 AccessDenied (the bucket root is also 403), and all Tumblr/Instagram URLs (78.media.tumblr.com, vt.media.tumblr.com, scontent.cdninstagram.com) return 000 in this environment. These are video/image content on index.html, breeze.html, scribbling-speech.html, and sensing-armband.html. The schema's type enum is only video|image (§3.3 line 219), so a Vimeo iframe fallback or an unavailable item has no representation. §2.2 also says 3 Tumblr pages; the repo has 2.
confirmed.suggestion: Audit all external URLs before Phase 2, record unrecoverable ones in media-audit.md, and define the fallback (remove with a note, placeholder, or owner-supplied replacement). If iframe fallbacks must remain, add an embed type or intentionally allow raw MDX HTML.

confirmed.issue: rclone sync is the only bulk-upload command, and it deletes destination-only objects, so uploading a partial media-out/ wipes previously uploaded project media.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.6 (lines 389-393) shows only rclone sync media-out/ r2:portfolio-media/. rclone sync --help on this machine states: 'Destination is updated to match source, including deleting files if necessary.' The bucket will hold roughly 450 MB and 300+ objects, and the design has no dry-run, prune step, versioning, or backup.
confirmed.suggestion: Use rclone copy for routine uploads and a separate, explicitly reviewed rclone sync --dry-run/delete step for pruning; enable R2 object versioning or use --backup-dir; require a complete media-out generation before any sync.

confirmed.issue: The rclone R2 remote is neither configured nor documented, and the stated bucket-scoped token cannot pass rclone's default bucket check unless no_check_bucket is set.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.6 (lines 384-393) says the token is scoped to portfolio-media (Object Read and Write) but shows only rclone sync media-out/ r2:portfolio-media/. On this machine rclone listremotes prints only gcs: (no r2:), and rclone config providers shows the S3 no_check_bucket default is False. Cloudflare's rclone documentation requires provider = Cloudflare, endpoint = https://<account_id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, region = auto, acl = private, and no_check_bucket = true for object-scoped tokens.
confirmed.suggestion: Document the exact rclone.conf block without secrets and add --s3-no-check-bucket; verify with rclone lsd r2:portfolio-media, and add --exclude .DS_Store to avoid uploading Finder junk.

confirmed.issue: Stable generic object keys plus a 7-day max-age mean that re-uploading a changed poster, video, or image serves stale content from Cloudflare's edge and from users' browsers; a dashboard purge is not a reliable invalidation path.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.1 (lines 302-310) uses fixed keys such as video-720.mp4, poster.jpg, and cover-2000.webp; §4.4 (lines 363-364) says 'Updates are rare and can be purged from the Cloudflare dashboard'; §9 (line 577) repeats the 7-day TTL/purge mitigation. Cloudflare's R2 custom-domain cache honors Cache-Control and does not invalidate warmed entries when an object key is overwritten; browser caches are outside any Cloudflare purge. rclone sync also does not re-upload unchanged objects, so a changed Cache-Control policy will not be applied to existing objects.
confirmed.suggestion: Version keys with a content hash (for example video-720.<hash>.mp4, or ?v=<hash> from the manifest) and use Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; otherwise shorten the TTL and purge changed URLs via the Cloudflare API from the upload script.

confirmed.section: §4.1 R2 layout / §4.6 Upload and credentials / §7 Phase 0
confirmed.issue: The R2 custom-domain prerequisites are incomplete: the bucket and the xinyue.de zone must be in the same Cloudflare account, and wrangler r2 bucket domain add requires a zone ID, neither of which the design pins.
confirmed.evidence: design.md §4.1 (lines 295-298) connects media.xinyue.de; §4.6 (line 382) says wrangler is 'already authenticated as xinyue@wordtoworld.io'; §7 Phase 0 (lines 494-497) still lists the nameserver migration as pending, but dig NS xinyue.de already returns sonia.ns.cloudflare.com and trevor.ns.cloudflare.com, and media.xinyue.de has no record. Cloudflare's command is wrangler r2 bucket domain add <BUCKET> --domain <domain> --zone-id <zone-id>, and the zone must be in the same account as the bucket. The design also says GitHub Pages records stay DNS-only without noting that the auto-created media record is proxied.

confirmed.issue: Astro's `redirects` config does not put the meta-refresh stub at the legacy `.html` path; it puts it at `dist/<legacy-path>/index.html`, so the design's stated redirect artifact and AC2 cannot be verified against the build.
confirmed.evidence: Reproduced with the exact 6.1 config (`site`, `build.format: 'directory'`, `trailingSlash: 'always'`, `redirects: {'/about/about.html': '/about/', '/breathing-surface.html': '/breathing-surface/'}`) on astro@5.18.2 and astro@7.4.1. The build reports `/about/about.html/index.html` and `/breathing-surface.html/index.html`; `dist/` contains `dist/about/about.html/index.html` and `dist/breathing-surface.html/index.html` but no `dist/about/about.html` and no `dist/breathing-surface.html`. The generated stub says `Redirecting from /about/about.html/`. Adding `public/about/about.html` to force the correct path collides with the redirect route and fails the build with `ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdir '.../dist/about/about.html/'`.
confirmed.suggestion: Remove the `.html` entries from `astro.config.mjs` and emit each legacy stub from `public/` (verified: with only public stubs, the build produces `dist/about/about.html` and `dist/breathing-surface.html` alongside `dist/about/index.html`), including the canonical link manually. Alternatively add a post-build script. Add a build assertion that every legacy path exists as a file in `dist/`, and test legacy URLs against GitHub Pages, not only a local server.

confirmed.issue: The toolchain versions are unpinned and the local Node version cannot run the current latest Astro, so Phase 1 fails on this machine.

Please upgrade Node.js to a supported version: >=22.22.0` (npm EBADENGINE reports >=22.19.0). The design says `Astro (latest stable)` and `Build: Node 22`.

confirmed.section: 9 Risks and rollback / 6.3 Branch and release
confirmed.issue: The documented rollback is not executable: a tag cannot be selected as a GitHub Pages source, and after merge `master` no longer contains the old site.
confirmed.evidence: Section 9 says `keep master untouched and tagged pre-astro ... set Pages back to the previous source and force-push nothing`; 6.3 creates the tag before merge; 3.2 says old source files are removed after verification. GitHub Pages' branch source selects a branch, not a tag. After merge, switching the source back to `master` publishes the new Astro site, and reverting the merge also removes `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, so Actions will not redeploy.
confirmed.suggestion: Create a `legacy-site` (or `gh-pages`) branch at the `pre-astro` commit and document exact rollback steps: switch Pages source to that branch, verify the old site, then fix forward. Keep this branch outside the history rewrite or archive it outside git.

confirmed.issue: The optional history rewrite invalidates the `pre-astro` tag that the rollback depends on.
confirmed.evidence: Phase 6 specifies `git filter-repo or BFG, a mirror backup, and a force push`; filter-repo rewrites every ref, so `pre-astro` would point to a commit whose media blobs have been stripped. The design does not say where the mirror backup lives or how restore is tested. GitHub reports `size: 527050` KB, 217 commits, 0 forks (`api.github.com/repos/softlipaschara/website`).
confirmed.suggestion: Before rewriting, create and verify an off-machine `git bundle`/mirror and archive the built old site; recreate tags after the rewrite and record backup location plus a restore test in `migration-checklist.md`.

confirmed.issue: The schema cannot supply the dimensions/aspect ratio or the 480p rendition that `ResponsivePicture` and `VideoPlayer` are specified to use.
confirmed.evidence: `media: { type, src, poster?, alt?, caption? }` and `cover: { src, alt }` (3.3) have no width/height/aspect ratio. 3.5 requires `ResponsivePicture` to emit `srcset` and `explicit dimensions`; 4.1/4.2 produce both `video-720.mp4` and `video-480.mp4`, but a media item has a single `src`. CI builds from a clean checkout and `media-out/` is gitignored (4.2), so the build cannot read the image files to derive dimensions.
confirmed.suggestion: Add width/height (or aspect ratio) to the schema and a generated build-time manifest, and add an explicit `sources` array or a documented naming convention for 480p/720p.

confirmed.issue: The Vimeo fallback and the old pages' interleaved text/media cannot be represented by the schema and `ProjectLayout` as specified.
confirmed.evidence: 4.7 says a video that cannot be obtained `keeps the original Vimeo iframe temporarily`, but the schema only allows `type: 'video' | 'image'` and `VideoPlayer` renders `<video>`. Old pages interleave text and media (`coffee-composer.html:42-47`; `word-to-world.html:59-124,145-211`), while 3.5 defines `ProjectLayout` as cover + title + tools + MDX body + media gallery. The design does not say whether the `media` array or the MDX body is authoritative or how MDX embeds get the R2 path/component treatment.
confirmed.suggestion: Define an `embed` media type or an explicit MDX escape hatch, and state whether project media live in frontmatter or as MDX-imported components; reconcile AC3's exception clause with the fallback.

confirmed.section: 2.2 Media inventory / 3.1 Stack / 3.6 Interaction preservation / 8 AC3
confirmed.issue: The external-reference audit and AC3 omit live third-party dependencies, and the carousel rewrite path is unspecified.
confirmed.evidence: `index.html:345-346`, `painting.html:6-7,98-99`, `photography.html:6-7,110-111`, and `printing.html:6-8,98-99` load jQuery and slick from `code.jquery.com`/`cdn.jsdelivr.net`; `contact/contact.html:6` loads font-awesome from `maxcdn.bootstrapcdn.com`; `paintings/indexpainting.html:7,10,12` loads Bootstrap from maxcdn; `index.html:324` embeds a Flash `.swf` from xiami.com. Section 2.2 lists only Vimeo/S3/Tumblr/Instagram/Google Fonts, and AC3 greps only those four domains. `carousel.js` is `$('.slider').slick({...})`, while 3.1 says `No client framework` and 3.6 promises exact carousel behavior.
confirmed.suggestion: Extend the audit and AC3 to every external origin, decide self-host vs vanilla rewrite for slick, and add a carousel acceptance case (arrows, dots, infinite, breakpoints, unslick at 300 px).

confirmed.section: 5.1 Layout rules vs 5.2 Desktop parity / 8 AC6
confirmed.issue: The responsive rules contradict desktop parity, and AC6 has no objective measurement protocol.
confirmed.evidence: 5.1 mandates `width: min(100% - 48px, 1200px)` and `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`; the old home is a full-width flex-wrap layout with `.center { width: 33% }` (`index.css:324-336`) and a full-bleed hero (`index.html:41-43`). Old breakpoints are 1280/1024/768/414/375/320 (`index.css:1093,1107,1115,1375,1659,1692`) vs new 640/900/1200; at exactly 1200 px the old site is in its `max-width: 1280px` branch while the new site is at its `min-width: 1200px` boundary. AC6 says `match` with no diff tool, threshold, page list, or protocol for animations/fonts/videos, and the migration intentionally repairs broken S3/Tumblr media, so screenshots will differ.
confirmed.suggestion: Express desktop rules as explicit per-page overrides, and define AC6 as a specific tool plus per-page diff ratio, stored baselines, and font/animation/video freeze rules; list intentionally repaired media as allowed differences.

confirmed.issue: Transparent GIFs and PNGs are flattened without a background/compositing rule, causing a visible parity regression.
confirmed.evidence: 19 of 50 GIFs contain fully transparent pixels (ffmpeg `alphaextract` min alpha 0; e.g. `imgA/cat.gif`, `imgA/grass.gif`), and 90 of 95 PNGs decode with an alpha channel. The GIF command `ffmpeg -i input.gif -vf 'scale=...' -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p ...` (4.2) has no composite step; H.264/`yuv420p` cannot carry alpha. The image pipeline (4.3) generates JPEG fallbacks with no stated flatten color. Page backgrounds are white (e.g. `index.css:309,564`), so transparent areas will render dark.
confirmed.suggestion: Composite onto the page background (for example a white `color`/`overlay` filter) before H.264 encoding, and either keep an alpha-capable fallback for transparent images or document the flatten color; add a visual check for the 19 affected GIFs.

confirmed.issue: Stable media filenames with a 7-day TTL have no way to invalidate browser caches.
confirmed.evidence: 4.1/4.4 use stable names (`video-720.mp4`, `cover-2000.webp`) with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800`; 4.4 says `Updates are rare and can be purged from the Cloudflare dashboard`. A Cloudflare purge does not clear browser caches, and `rclone sync` does not purge Cloudflare. There is no purge script or changed-object list.
confirmed.suggestion: Use content-hashed filenames or a version query in frontmatter, and add an automated purge step (Cloudflare API token) or a documented per-object purge list to the upload script.

confirmed.issue: `rclone sync` can delete live objects, and `verify a sample` cannot prove upload completeness.
confirmed.evidence: The command is `rclone sync media-out/ r2:portfolio-media/ ...`, which deletes remote objects absent locally; `media-out/` is gitignored and regenerated, so a partial transcode run deletes production objects. Phase 3's only check is `verify a sample of objects over HTTPS`.
confirmed.suggestion: Use `rclone copy` plus an explicit prune (or run `--dry-run` first), enable R2 object versioning, and replace the sample check with an automated HEAD/GET of every media URL referenced by `dist/`.

confirmed.issue: AC7 assumes the build checks internal links, but no link checker is specified; the resume PDF is missing from the asset inventory and would 404.
confirmed.evidence: `astro build` does not validate `<a href>` targets, and the design lists no link-checker dependency or CI step. `index.html:230` links `imgA/resume_xinyue_2020.pdf`; 2.2's table covers only mp4/gif/jpg/png/mov, and 4.1 has no PDF slot. Also tracked but unaddressed: `font/HiraKakuInterface-W1.otf` (3.5 MB, no references), `font/HelveticaNeue.dfont` (6.4 MB, no references), and four `.DS_Store` files.
confirmed.suggestion: Add a link checker (lychee/linkinator or a Playwright crawl) against the served `dist/`, scoped to internal links; add the resume PDF and the unused/tracked files to `media-audit.md` and decide keep/remove.

confirmed.issue: The Pages source is switched after the merge, so the first Actions deploy cannot succeed.
confirmed.evidence: 6.2 says the workflow triggers on `push to master` and that Settings -> Pages -> Source = GitHub Actions is a one-time manual change; Phase 5 says `Merge to master, enable GitHub Actions as the Pages source, and confirm the production deploy`. `actions/deploy-pages` requires the Pages site to use the Actions build type, so the push-triggered run happens before the source change.
confirmed.suggestion: Switch the Pages source to GitHub Actions before the merge (or before pushing the workflow commit), then merge; use `workflow_dispatch` for re-runs and make AC8 `the first post-switch run deploys successfully`.

confirmed.section: 1 Background and goals / 9 Risks and rollback
confirmed.issue: The stated mainland-China reachability motivation is undermined by keeping the HTML site on GitHub Pages.
confirmed.evidence: Section 1 says Vimeo is `unreachable from mainland China`; 4.1/9 keep GitHub Pages records DNS-only and make R2 the only media origin. GitHub Pages is itself frequently unreachable in mainland China, and Cloudflare's free plan for `media.xinyue.de` routes to overseas points of presence. Section 5.4 self-hosts fonts for this reason, but 1/9 never acknowledge that the page itself may not load.
confirmed.suggestion: Add this residual risk to the table and define the success test (a request from a mainland network), or explicitly scope the goal to media only; consider a Cloudflare-proxied HTML origin or mirror if reachability is required.

confirmed.issue: The repo-size goal is not met by the migration; it depends on the optional Phase 6.
confirmed.evidence: Goal 1 cites the 460 MB working tree and 528 MB `.git`; Phase 6 is `Optional history cleanup ... After the new site is live and stable`. Removing `imgA/` from HEAD does not shrink `.git`; GitHub reports `size: 527050` KB (API). No acceptance criterion measures repo size.
confirmed.suggestion: Add a hard AC (for example `.git` size and `no tracked file > 10 MB` after the rewrite), commit the old-media deletion in the rebuild PR, and either make Phase 6 required or stop claiming goal 1 is achieved.

confirmed.issue: `.gitignore` does not cover the new build/media directories, and the actual `media-src` path differs from the design.
confirmed.evidence: `.gitignore` contains only `.idea/` and `.DS_Store`; `media-src/`, `media-out/`, `public/media/` (4.5), `node_modules/`, and `dist/` are not ignored. `localize.sh` copies roughly 350 MB into `public/media/`. The downloaded sources are at `/Users/xiaoxia/Development/portfolio/media-src`, outside the repo, not `website/media-src` as 2.2/4.2 imply.
confirmed.suggestion: Add `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `public/media/`, `media-out/`, and `.env*` to `.gitignore` in Phase 1, and correct the `media-src` location in the design and scripts.

minor.issue: `legacyPath` is required for every project but consumed nowhere, while legacy routes are hand-maintained in astro.config.mjs; the two can drift, and `draft` is likewise never filtered.
minor.evidence: design.md §3.3 declares `legacyPath: z.string()` and `draft: z.boolean().default(false)`; §3.4 hardcodes legacy redirects in astro.config.mjs ("one entry per project page"); neither §3.5 nor the getStaticPaths description reads either field. Astro config is evaluated before content collections load, so redirects cannot be derived from the collection there.
minor.suggestion: Either remove both fields, or generate redirects from the collection with a prerendered endpoint/integration (the verified `src/pages/[...legacy].ts` pattern emits exact `dist/<legacy>.html` files), and filter drafts in getStaticPaths.

minor.issue: UI assets placed in `public/` are not fingerprinted by Astro, so the caching claim is false.
minor.evidence: design.md §4.1 keeps favicon/back button/logos/fonts in `public/assets/ui/`; §4.4 says "Astro fingerprints filenames". An Astro 7.4.1 build with `public/assets/ui/test.css` emitted `dist/assets/ui/test.css` unchanged, since public files are copied verbatim.
minor.suggestion: Move hashable assets to `src/assets/` and import them, or state that public URLs are stable and set cache policy accordingly.

minor.issue: Phase 2 is not a mechanical HTML-to-MDX conversion: several legacy attributes are invalid JSX and fail the MDX compiler.
minor.evidence: `coffee-composer.html:64` has `<video ... width=100%; >`; `scribbling-speech.html:102` has `poster="..."autoplay=...` with no separating space; `word-to-world.html:59` has a stray `"` before `src`; `painting.html` has a duplicated `</head>` and a `<style>` block after it. Compiling the coffee-composer video line as MDX produced `Unexpected character after '<', expected a valid JSX tag (mdx-jsx:unexpected-character)`.
minor.suggestion: Add an HTML normalization/tidy step before MDX conversion and require a per-page build in the migration checklist.

minor.issue: The design says "Astro (latest stable)" without pinning, and imports `z` from `astro:content`, which Astro 7.4.1 marks as a compatibility re-export scheduled for removal in Astro 8.
minor.evidence: `npm view astro version` returns 7.4.1 and `@astrojs/mdx` returns 8.1.0. Astro 7.4.1's content virtual module template contains `// TODO: remove in Astro 8` immediately above `export { z } from 'astro/zod'`; design.md §3.3 uses `import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content'`.
minor.suggestion: Pin exact Astro and @astrojs/mdx versions and commit the lockfile; import `z` from `astro/zod`.

minor.issue: TypeScript setup is unspecified and unverified, and the "TypeScript for scripts" claim does not match the media scripts.
minor.evidence: design.md §3.2 lists `tsconfig.json` with no preset and includes `scripts/media/audit.mjs` plus shell scripts; §3.1 says "TypeScript for scripts and content schema"; §6.2 runs only `npm ci` and `npm run build`, which do not type-check, and `astro check` is absent from §8.
minor.suggestion: Extend `astro/tsconfigs/strict`, add `astro check` to CI, and either convert the media scripts or narrow the TypeScript claim.

minor.issue: The statement that long-lived caching of UI assets "is handled by GitHub Pages defaults" is false. GitHub Pages serves CSS, JS, and images with `Cache-Control: max-age=600` (10 minutes), including fingerprinted files.
minor.evidence: Live checks: `curl -I https://xinyue.de/index.css`, `/hideContent.js`, and `/imgA/favicon.png` all return `cache-control: max-age=600` with `expires` 10 minutes later. The design configures no Pages caching.
minor.suggestion: Correct the caching claim and decide whether 10-minute caching is acceptable; long-lived immutable caching would require serving `public/assets` through Cloudflare/R2 or proxying Pages, which conflicts with the DNS-only setup in 4.1.

minor.issue: The design specifies "Concurrency group `pages`, cancel in progress". GitHub's official Pages starter uses `cancel-in-progress: false` specifically so an in-flight production deployment can complete; cancelling can leave the live site on the previous version.
minor.evidence: `actions/starter-workflows/pages/static.yml` uses `concurrency: {group: 'pages', cancel-in-progress: false}` with the comment "do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete." Design 6.2 says "cancel in progress" and does not specify whether concurrency is workflow- or job-level.
minor.suggestion: Use `cancel-in-progress: false` at the workflow level (matching the official starter) and document that the newest push waits for the active deployment.

minor.issue: The launch checklist omits two custom-domain checks: "Enforce HTTPS" is currently off (`http://xinyue.de` returns 200 with no redirect), and there is no post-switch verification that the custom domain survived the Pages source change. Phase 0 also still lists the Cloudflare nameserver migration as pending even though the zone is already on Cloudflare NS.
minor.evidence: `curl -sI http://xinyue.de` returns `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with no `Location`. `dig NS xinyue.de` returns `trevor.ns.cloudflare.com` and `sonia.ns.cloudflare.com`; apex A records are 185.199.108-111.153 and `www` is a CNAME to `softlipaschara.github.io`; `media.xinyue.de` does not resolve. Design 4.1 says the zone is hosted on Cloudflare, while Phase 0 says "Complete the xinyue.de nameserver migration to Cloudflare."
minor.suggestion: After switching to Actions, verify Settings > Pages still shows `xinyue.de` and enable Enforce HTTPS; update Phase 0 to a DNS verification item and keep only `media.xinyue.de` as pending.

minor.issue: Moving media to `projects/<slug>/...` breaks all old media and asset URLs (`https://xinyue.de/imgA/...`, root `index.css`, `js/*`). The "keep existing URLs working" goal and acceptance criterion 2 cover only the 27 page routes; after old files are removed, indexed or hotlinked media URLs return 404. Cloudflare redirect rules cannot fix this while the apex is DNS-only.
minor.evidence: Design 4.1 object paths are `projects/<slug>/video-720.mp4`, etc.; design 2.2 counts 60 mp4, 50 gif, 93 jpg, 95 png and says `imgA/` is 449 MB. Existing pages reference `imgA/...` (for example `index.html` lines 62-281), and `https://xinyue.de/imgA/favicon.png` is live today. Design 4.1 says GitHub Pages records remain DNS-only.
minor.suggestion: Decide explicitly: accept and document media-URL breakage, or keep the old files for the most-linked assets; arbitrary legacy media redirects are only possible by proxying the apex through Cloudflare or keeping the files on Pages.

minor.issue: The reference ffmpeg commands omit -y, so rerunning the pipeline with existing outputs silently keeps the old media.
minor.evidence: design.md §4.2 (lines 331-347) shows ffmpeg without -y. Running the transcode command twice locally prints 'File ... already exists. Overwrite? [y/N] Not overwriting - exiting' and returns exit code 0 while leaving the first output in place; rclone sync then uploads the stale file.
minor.suggestion: Add -y to every ffmpeg command and clean or atomically replace media-out before each run.

minor.issue: The transcode and image pipelines upscale low-resolution sources and do not enforce the stated 48 kHz audio format.
